notes:
Demand is built person-by-person from Chilean government household travel surveys (Encuesta Origen-Destino, SECTRA / Ministerio de Transportes). Each surveyed household carries a geocoded home address; each person carries a geocoded workplace or place of study plus a weekday expansion factor. One game pop = one surveyed person's home-to-work or home-to-study trip at their survey weight, scaled to the game's demand basis. No gravity model is used.

Surveys, all with per-person geocoded origin and destination:
- EOD Santiago 2012, official 2017 census re-expansion, 11,230 weekday households in bbox
- EOD Gran Valparaiso 2014, 7,152 households
- EOD San Antonio 2017, 1,687 households

Each survey region is scaled to its own represented population, so neither end of the map dominates the other. Cross-region commuting is real where the surveys recorded it: the Valparaiso survey codes destinations in the Region Metropolitana as external zones, giving 19,465 daily commuters into Santiago and 8,983 the other way.

Residence anchoring: Censo 2017 manzana (city block) microdata from INE, 63,618 blocks in bbox. Checked for suppression: comuna sums match published comuna totals exactly (e.g. Colina 146,207, Lampa 102,034), so no loss at block grain. Where the 2012 survey under-represents an area that has since grown (Chicureo, Batuco, Polpaico), synthetic households are added to match census block counts, cloned from nearby surveyed households matched on reported income. Comuna totals are preserved. This affects about 3% of the map.

Towns inside the bbox that no EOD covers (Quillota, Casablanca, Curacavi, El Quisco, Algarrobo, Cartagena, El Tabo, Santo Domingo) have residents placed from Censo 2017 blocks, with commute patterns cloned from the nearest surveyed households of similar income - San Antonio households for the southern coast, Valparaiso households for the north. El Quisco and Algarrobo have no nearby donor and commute locally by assumption.

Employment rate of 0.41 where census-derived employed residents are needed, derived independently from two surveys (Santiago 0.409, Valparaiso 0.429).

Vintages: residence Censo 2017; workplace EOD 2012 / 2014 / 2017; buildings Overture/OSM 2026.

Known limitations: the Santiago survey is 2012 fieldwork re-expanded to 2017 population. Trip purposes are limited to work and study, which is what the game's demand model represents. — Reviewer refinements (2026-09-07): resident_count re-ruled total_population — the census manzana microdata counts total population; employed residents are derived by a single flat employment rate (0.41, survey-derived and disclosed by the author), so the origin anchor is a total-population count, not a measured per-block employed-resident count (the rungs price exactly the spatial employment variation a flat scalar cannot carry). workplace_granularity and od_granularity re-ruled adm3 — EOD workplaces and flows are geocoded but sample-thin (11,230 households Santiago 2012 / 7,152 Valparaiso 2014 / 1,687 San Antonio 2017); job totals and flow cells are statistically supported at comuna grain, which is also where the census re-expansion and all validation are calibrated (comuna totals preserved). The manzana resident anchoring keeps adm5 with mesh_125_or_adm5 x measured_per_unit as filed (suppression cross-check on record). workplace_count kept physical_measured — the EOD directly measures each surveyed person's physical workplace (the form label includes surveys); the sampling penalty is priced once, on the granularity axis (vienna single-axis precedent). od_metric kept full_matrix at the adm3 grain — three-survey coverage with observed cross-region flows via the Valparaiso survey's external zones (19,465 / 8,983 daily); the donor-cloned coastal towns (Quillota, Casablanca, Curacavi, El Quisco, Algarrobo, Cartagena, El Tabo, Santo Domingo) are a small demand share, recorded as the exception.
